The three core primitives—play-level analytics, projection kernel, and DVOA metric—form a hierarchical mathematical model where low-level play data is aggregated into higher-order statistical summaries. The play-level kernel provides granular event tracking, while the projection kernel synthesizes these into forecasts. DVOA serves as a derived measure of relative strength, enabling both GSI’s probabilistic inference and GSE’s strategic planning. These operators exhibit duality in their application: play-level data informs projections, which in turn validate DVOA accuracy. Failure modes include data latency, inconsistent labeling, or misalignment between projection models and actual outcomes, particularly during high-variance periods such as playoffs or injury disruptions.
